checks.item: A diarizer load failure cannot take down the socket
checks.evidence: Services.make_backend is called inside ConversationState.__init__ (stream.py:78) with no try/except, and create_app builds that state inside the websocket handler (app.py:20). If make_backend raises, as PyannoteBackend() does by design until the terms are accepted, the handler raises and the connection dies. Nothing is cached, so every later connection to that conversation does the same. I reproduced it with my own test, test_make_backend_failure_does_not_kill_socket, using make_backend=lambda: raise RuntimeError: the traceback ends at stream.py:78 and the websocket fails instead of sending 'recording'. No test in the repo covers this.

failures: A diarizer backend that fails to load takes down the websocket. src/contextlens/api/stream.py:78 calls svc.make_backend() in ConversationState.__init__ with no handling, and src/contextlens/api/app.py:20 runs that inside the websocket handler. PyannoteBackend() raises RuntimeError by design until the person accepts the community-1 terms, so any wiring of make_backend=PyannoteBackend would make every connection fail. The plan check says a load failure must not take down the socket and turns must stay unknown. Reproduce: build Services(..., make_backend=lambda: (_ for _ in ()).throw(RuntimeError('x'))), connect to /ws/c1, and the handler raises instead of sending status recording. Expected: catch the failure, log only the exception type, continue with backend=None (turns unknown), and add a test.
notes: Real diarization is unproven at this commit. The pyannote adapter has never run (it is blocked on the community-1 gated repo terms), and tests/test_diarize_real.py is skipped with the reason. T8.7 owns the real run (PLAN lines 331-332). The background assignment logic is tested only with a fake backend. docs/datasets.md records the choice (pyannote 3.1) and what is blocked. Live speaker updates to clients are routed to T8.7: the plan adds a turn-update message there, and turns are sent as unknown and relabelled only in the store. Memory items extracted while a turn was unknown keep that label (PLAN line 314). Production wiring of make_backend, make_assistant and the Postgres store is also T8.7's. Minor: the epoch check and feed() are not atomic against wipe() on another connection, so a very narrow window exists, but the epoch guard on ingest and the stream-epoch check bound it; this is not a failure. A timed-out assistant thread keeps running after wait_for gives up, so many hung presses could pile up threads, though the socket stays responsive. The other connections to a deleted conversation get no 'deleted' status, only the one that sent delete does, which the contract allows. The only failure found is the one listed; fixing it and adding a test should be enough for a PASS.
